crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Self-Driving Laboratories
children.blurb: Self-driving laboratories are research systems that combine robotic automation, laboratory instruments, and artificial intelligence to run experiments with limited human intervention.

children.name: Digital Twins for Experiments
children.blurb: Digital twins for experiments are computational models of a physical experiment, instrument, or sample that stay synchronized with real data.

children.name: Instrument and Sensor Data
children.blurb: Instrument and sensor data is the stream of measurements that laboratory instruments and sensors produce, together with the context that makes those measurements meaningful.

children.name: Optimising Lab Protocols
children.blurb: Optimising lab protocols covers the design, scheduling, and revision of experimental procedures so that they use less time, reagent, and labour while producing more reliable results.

children.name: Forecasting Lab Supplies
children.blurb: Forecasting lab supplies covers the prediction of demand for reagents, consumables, kits, and other materials that a laboratory consumes during routine and project work.

sections.body: Laboratory automation and simulation is the use of AI to run experiments, model physical systems, and manage the flow of materials and data in research labs. In practice, AI schedules robotic liquid handlers, chooses next experiments, and adjusts parameters based on incoming measurements. Digital twins combine physics models with sensor data to predict how an experiment will behave before it is run. Instrument and sensor data pipelines turn raw signals into structured measurements that learning algorithms can use. Protocol optimisation searches over reagent amounts, timings, and temperatures to find reliable conditions. Supply forecasting predicts when consumables will run low so that experiments are not interrupted, and these systems are connected rather than isolated.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are mature, and robotic liquid handling and scheduling software are widely used in industrial and academic labs. Digital twins work well for well-characterised physical systems, such as thermal or fluidic test beds, but they struggle when biology or chemistry is poorly understood. Protocol optimisation can improve yield and reproducibility on defined assays, yet it often needs many experiments and may not transfer to new contexts. Instrument data integration remains fragmented because vendors use different formats and interfaces. Supply forecasting is limited by unreliable delivery data and by the fact that many labs do not track inventory in a consistent way. Full self-driving labs that close the loop from hypothesis to experiment to analysis are rare and usually operate in narrow domains.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The page on Self-Driving Laboratories gives the broadest view, covering closed-loop systems that plan, run, and interpret experiments. Digital Twins for Experiments explains how virtual models are built and validated against real apparatus. Instrument and Sensor Data covers the acquisition layer, including calibration, noise, and data standards. Optimising Lab Protocols focuses on experimental design and parameter search, including Bayesian optimisation and related methods. Forecasting Lab Supplies addresses inventory, lead times, and demand prediction for consumables and reagents. Together these pages move from physical execution to virtual representation to data handling to decision making to logistics, and for readers who want primary sources, the site's library holds 135 research papers, with pages linking to original papers rather than to the Consensus search tool.
